title: How to Do the Waka Waka | Hip-Hop Dancing

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher breaks down the dance into small, manageable segments, focusing on feet and arms separately before combining them. She uses a friendly, encouraging tone and provides clear, step-by-step instructions.

lesson_structure.note: The teacher introduces the dance and herself.
The teacher breaks down the footwork.
The teacher breaks down the arm movements.
The teacher adds the chest movement.
The teacher explains how to coordinate the waist with the arms and legs.
The teacher performs the dance with music.

metaphors: hands placed here like you're praying

steps_taught.name: Waka Waka chorus
steps_taught.description: A sequence involving specific footwork, arm movements, and chest pushes.

what_works: The teacher breaks down the movements into small, manageable parts.
The teacher demonstrates the steps slowly before speeding up.
what_hinders: The teacher does not provide a mirror-image view, which can make it harder for the student to follow along.

quotes.text: Let's focus on the feet first because she's super specific.
It's a little hard to separate them.
Hands placed here like you're praying.
Your waist just goes with your arms and with your legs.

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher demonstrates the footwork by stepping forward with the right foot, then back with the left foot.
The teacher moves her hands from side to side.
The teacher demonstrates the chest push from the side.
The teacher combines the footwork and arm movements.
The teacher demonstrates the waist movement.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher explicitly separates the footwork and arm movements before combining them, which is a common but effective teaching method for beginners.
